title: Tight adaptive CCA frontier for multi-round CLRW
summary: Determine the tight adaptive CCA exponent of chained LRW for every round count above two, including the conjectured round-dependent bound.

formal_statement.body: For every fixed integer $r>2$, determine the tight adaptive bidirectional CCA query-security frontier of the $r$-round chained LRW construction with independent round block-cipher and AXU-hash keys; in particular, prove or refute the conjectured exponent $rn/(r+1)$ by matching security and attack bounds.

scope.domain: Multi-round cascades of LRW tweakable-block-cipher constructions under adaptive CCA.
assumptions: Each round uses independent block-cipher and AXU-hash keys.
The adversary has adaptive chosen-plaintext and chosen-ciphertext access.
scope.unresolved_remainder: A later result gives roughly $2^{3n/4}$ security for the relevant cascaded LRW family, but the conjectured $2^{rn/(r+1)}$ frontier is not matched for every $r>2$.

provenance.note: The 2015 paper explicitly attributes the conjecture to Lampe and Seurin; the FSE proceedings text contains the same Open Problems statement.

progress.summary: The TEM paper recalls tight multi-round CLRW analysis as the natural antecedent to its own conjecture.
A cascaded-LRW analysis proves a roughly $2^{3n/4}$ security level for the relevant family while leaving the general round-dependent exponent unmatched.
